parsed.explanation: No trans-specific entry restriction, no facility ban, no criminalisation of expression; the state's strongest documented exposures are resident-facing (public health care access, adolescent care) or require arrest. Custody policy is genuinely protective on paper — self-declaration before a judge, preference-based placement, LGBTI units — and the operational gap (one state prison census showing trans women in male units) is documented practice but reachable only after arrest, so it is a real but narrower exposure. Courts are documented working FOR trans people: the moral-damage award against a nightclub, extension of the femicide law, criminalised transphobia, bathroom guidance. The violence record is undated and undominated — no denominators, no trans-specific homicide data — so it reads as societal friction plus background crime, not a campaign. Above the 0.65 tier for functioning remedies; below 0.85 because the practice gap and hostile mobilisation are documented, not extrapolated.
